tytul: Quince paste (membrillo) for the refrigerator or freezer
wstep: This card follows the Food Preserving recipe for quince paste (dulce de membrillo): quince purée cooked with sugar for about 3 hours until thick, set in the refrigerator, then sliced and wrapped.

ostrzezenia.tekst: The source allows up to 3 months in the refrigerator, but this is not a tested recipe: University of Wisconsin Extension says untested recipes can be prepared and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, and not on the counter.

akapity: It covers paste kept in the refrigerator or freezer, not paste canned in jars.
The US FDA list gives fresh or stewed quince an approximate pH of 3.12–3.40.
2.5 kg of quinces, 2 1/2 cups of water and 1/3 cup of lemon juice.
About 1 kg of sugar: 3/4 to 1 cup of sugar for each cup of purée.
The recipe uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.
Cook and purée the quinces as the source directs; this card gives only the quantities, cooking time and storage checked against it.
Measure the purée, add the sugar and cook for about 3 hours until thick.
Pour the paste into a dish and let it set in the refrigerator for 12–24 hours.
Slice the paste and wrap it in plastic wrap, or store it in airtight containers.
Keep the paste in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks and do not store it on the counter.
According to the source, the paste can also be frozen for up to 12 months.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep the paste on the middle shelf of the refrigerator, not in the door: Wisconsin Extension assumes 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder for refrigerator pickles, while a Polish sanitary inspection office gives about 10 °C for the door, even though it suggests the door for jars of preserves.
